This page helps you find the function for a task and the methods that read
its result. It explains how the names are built, then lists the functions by
task and the methods by result. It runs no analysis. The guides that use these
functions run on [The Cornwall GP example data](cornwall-data.html). The
`spax()` interface and the allocation model are experimental and may change in
later versions.

## How the names work

The prefix says what a function is for, and the rest names the thing:

- `spax()` runs a model specification on prepared data: a method of the
  two-step floating catchment area (2SFCA) family, which gives accessibility
  scores, or an allocation model. `spax_<model>()` runs one model in one call
  from raw inputs: `spax_e2sfca()` and the other 2SFCA-family methods,
  `spax_huff()` and `spax_clm()`.
- `prep_` prepares data: `prep_data()`.
- `spec_` specifies a model without data: `spec_clm()` (the conditional logit
  model, CLM: facilities plus an outside option, the choice of none of them),
  `spec_huff()` (the Huff model: facilities only) and the 2SFCA-family
  methods `spec_2sfca()`, `spec_e2sfca()`, `spec_m2sfca()`, `spec_3sfca()` and
  `spec_huff2sfca()`, compared in [Which 2SFCA method?](fca-methods.html).
- `decay_` declares how weight falls with travel time: `decay_gaussian()`,
  `decay_exponential()`, `decay_power()`, `decay_custom()` and
  `decay_kernel()`. `decay_step()` and `decay_inverse()` are for 2SFCA-family
  methods only.
- `obs_` declares observed counts: `obs_flows()` and `obs_totals()`.
- `calc_`, `gather_` and `spread_` are the building blocks of an
  accessibility score.
  `calc_travel_time()` and `calc_demand()` compute inputs.
- `transform_`, `rasterize_`, `update_` and `sample_` move area totals onto a
  grid, and `read_` and `save_` read and write files.
- `<verb>_allocation()` are the steps that `spax()` runs underneath for an
  allocation model, such as `fit_allocation()`.

A model keeps its name as the suffix: `spec_huff()` specifies the Huff model,
and `spax_huff()` runs it. `check_fit()`, `compare_fits()` and `bootstrap_fit()`
work on fitted results: a result of `spax()`, or a model and its fit from the
steps. They are also named `check_allocation()`, `compare_allocations()` and
`bootstrap_allocation()`: each pair is one function.

## Find a function by task

Every exported function appears on this page, most of them in this table.

| Task | Functions | What you get |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Read the example grids | `read_spax_example()` | A population or travel raster |
| Prepare inputs for any model | `prep_data()` | Prepared data: numeric inputs, or raster data |
| Spread area totals over a grid | `transform_pmf()`, `transform_demand()` | A grid of shares that sum to 1 (`transform_pmf()`), or with `density = TRUE` counts that keep each area's total (`transform_demand()`) |
| Reweight a grid pattern by an area rate | `rasterize_demand()`, or its parts `transform_likelihood()` and `update_pmf()` | A grid of shares or of counts |
| Draw random point patterns from a grid | `sample_pmf()` | Counts per cell, one layer per draw |
| Compute travel times over a friction surface | `calc_travel_time()` | A travel matrix or raster |
| Compute demand from population groups and rates | `calc_demand()` | A demand raster or vector |
| Compute accessibility scores | `spax()` with `spec_2sfca()`, `spec_e2sfca()`, `spec_m2sfca()`, `spec_3sfca()` or `spec_huff2sfca()` | On raster data, a `spax` result with the accessibility map; on numeric data, the score at each origin |
| Compute accessibility scores in one call | `spax_2sfca()`, `spax_e2sfca()`, `spax_m2sfca()`, `spax_3sfca()`, `spax_huff2sfca()` | A `spax` result with the accessibility map |
| Choose the decay of a 2SFCA-family method | `decay_gaussian()`, `decay_exponential()` or `decay_power()` with a number or a raster `sigma`; `decay_step()`, `decay_inverse()`, `decay_custom()` | A decay for the specification |
| Build accessibility scores from their parts | `calc_decay()`, `calc_normalize()`, `calc_choice()`, `gather_weighted()`, `gather_demand()`, `spread_weighted()`, `spread_access()`, `compute_access()` | Weights, demand per facility and rasters of scores |
| Save and read an accessibility map with its rasters | `save_spax()`, `read_spax()` | Files on disk, and the result read back |
| Specify an allocation model | `spec_clm()`, `spec_huff()` with `decay_gaussian()`, `decay_exponential()`, `decay_power()` or `decay_custom()` | A model specification |
| Declare a decay curve of your own | `decay_kernel()`, used through `decay_custom()` | A kernel declaration |
| Declare observed counts | `obs_flows()`, `obs_totals()` | Observed counts with the loss that fits them |
| Fit an allocation model, or run it at fixed parameter values | `spax()`; from raw inputs in one call, `spax_clm()` or `spax_huff()` | An allocation result |
| Predict at other origins | `predict()` on an allocation result | Probabilities, outside shares and flows by origin |
| Check what the data identify | `check_fit()` | The fit beside simpler allocations |
| Compare fitted models | `compare_fits()` | One row per fit |
| Put intervals on a fit to facility totals | `bootstrap_fit()` | Estimates, intervals and every attempt |
| Run the allocation steps one at a time | `prepare_allocation()`, `clm_allocation()`, `huff_allocation()`, `fit_allocation()`, `evaluate_allocation()`, `predict_allocation()` | Prepared inputs, a declared model, a fit, an evaluation or a prediction |

```{r public-interface-check, include = FALSE}
# Every function named on this page is exported, and every export is named
functions <- c(
  "read_spax_example", "prep_data", "transform_pmf", "transform_demand",
  "rasterize_demand", "transform_likelihood", "update_pmf", "sample_pmf",
  "calc_travel_time", "calc_demand",
  "spax", "spec_2sfca", "spec_e2sfca", "spec_m2sfca", "spec_3sfca",
  "spec_huff2sfca", "spax_2sfca", "spax_e2sfca", "spax_m2sfca", "spax_3sfca",
  "spax_huff2sfca", "decay_gaussian", "decay_exponential", "decay_power",
  "decay_step", "decay_inverse", "decay_custom", "calc_decay",
  "calc_normalize", "calc_choice", "gather_weighted", "gather_demand",
  "spread_weighted", "spread_access", "compute_access", "save_spax",
  "read_spax",
  "spec_clm", "spec_huff", "decay_kernel", "obs_flows", "obs_totals",
  "spax_clm", "spax_huff", "check_fit", "check_allocation", "compare_fits",
  "compare_allocations", "bootstrap_fit", "bootstrap_allocation",
  "prepare_allocation", "clm_allocation", "huff_allocation", "fit_allocation",
  "evaluate_allocation", "predict_allocation"
)
exported <- getNamespaceExports("spax")
not_exported <- setdiff(functions, exported)
not_listed <- setdiff(exported, functions)
if (length(not_exported)) {
  stop("Function map names functions that are not exported: ",
       paste(not_exported, collapse = ", "))
}
if (length(not_listed)) {
  stop("Function map leaves out exported functions: ",
       paste(not_listed, collapse = ", "))
}
```

## Read a result

Each result has methods that read it. None of them refits the model or
resamples the bootstrap. An output that a fit did not keep, such as the flows
of a fit to facility totals, is computed when you ask for it.

| Result | Made by | Read it with |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Accessibility map on a grid (`spax`) | `spax()` on raster data, `spax_e2sfca()` and the other one-call functions | `print()`, `summary()`, `plot()`; `$accessibility` is the raster of scores |
| Accessibility scores on numeric data (`spax_access_values`) | `spax()` on numeric data | `print()`, `summary()`, `as.data.frame()`; `$access` is a matrix with one row per origin |
| Allocation result (`spax_allocation`) | `spax()`, `spax_clm()`, `spax_huff()` | `print()`, `summary()`, `coef()`, `fitted()`, `predict()`, `as.data.frame()` with `type` `"parameters"`, `"facilities"`, `"origins"`, `"flows"` or `"starts"` |
| Prediction | `predict()`, `predict_allocation()` | `print()`; `$outputs` holds what you asked for; `$validity` gives each origin a status, such as `valid`, `unknown_travel` or `known_absence`, saying whether its values could be computed |
| Check | `check_fit()` | `print()`, `as.data.frame()` |
| Comparison | `compare_fits()` | `print()`, `as.data.frame()` with `type` `"fits"` or `"zones"` |
| Bootstrap | `bootstrap_fit()` | `print()`, `summary()`, `plot()` with `quantity` and `type` `"interval"` or `"draws"`, `as.data.frame()` with `type` `"estimates"`, `"draws"` or `"starts"` |
| Fit from the steps (`ae_multistart_fit`), also `$fit` of an allocation result | `fit_allocation()` | `print()`, `summary()`, `coef()`, `fitted()`, `as.data.frame()`, `plot()` with `type` `"fit"`, `"convergence"` or `"state"`, and `main`, `xlab` and `ylab` for your own labels |

A raster of scores is read with terra, for example `terra::values()` or
`terra::as.data.frame()`. [Reading results](reading-results.html) says how to
save each kind of result.
